newsitem.title: USA: Hatch says Justice's Klein "highly qualified".
newsitem.headline: Hatch says Justice's Klein "highly qualified".

text.p: Senate Judiciary Chairman Orrin Hatch believes Joel Klein is "highly qualified" to be the chief of the Justice Department's antitrust division, a spokeswoman for the Utah Republican said Tuesday.
President Clinton has all but settled on Klein to replace Anne Bingaman as antitrust chief in the Justice Department, Reuters reported Monday. Klein is now acting head of the division.
The spokeswoman for Hatch said the Utah Republican "holds Mr. Klein in very high regard; he considers him one of the finest legal minds in washington.

"And (Hatch) feels he (Klein) is a superb lawyer who is highly qualified to be the antitrust chief," the spokeswoman said. "He knows of no serious confirmation battle in the Senate regarding Mr. Klein."
Hatch's opinion is of key importance, because his committee reviews presidential nominations for Justice Department positions which require Senate confirmation.
In addition, Hatch's strong backing would likely be enough to reassure other conservative members of the Senate.
The Justice Department had no comment on Hatch's remarks.
